title: Send SignalR notifications per project
summary: Task updates go to every client. Scope them to a group. Joining from the client is lost when a reconnect brings a new connection ID, so the server decides membership in OnConnectedAsync.

turns.user: task update notifications go to literally everyone rn. people are complaining about projects theyre not even in

assistant.body: Let's use SignalR groups. Add JoinProject to the hub and put the calling connection's ID in a group named project:{id}. On the sending side, Clients.All becomes Clients.Group. Once the client calls JoinProject when the page opens, it only receives that project's notifications from then on.

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect. Groups belong to connection IDs, and SignalR drops a connection from every group when it closes. withAutomaticReconnect comes back with a new connection ID, so it is in no group at all. Stateful reconnect, added in ASP.NET Core 8.0, is off by default. There is a second problem: JoinProject accepts any projectId, so anyone can join a project they are not in. The fix is to stop trusting the client and let the server decide in OnConnectedAsync from the memberships in the database. It runs on every connection, reconnects included.

assistant.body: Sure. The membership query drops Guest. Caveat: there is no API to remove a user from a group, only a connection, so a guest who is connected right now stays in the group until they disconnect.
sed -i '' 's/\.Where(m => m\.UserId == userId)/.Where(m => m.UserId == userId \&\& m.Role != MemberRole.Guest)/' src/Notifications/NotificationHub.cs
